cards.explanation: The answer is his plea for mercy, friends. He says, "O Lord, hear my voice; let Your ears be attentive to my plea for mercy." He's down in the depths and he doesn't show up with a speech. He just asks for mercy, plain and simple. I respect that, because I've never once gotten out of a tight spot by sounding fancy.

The answer is False, friends. The question is "…who, O Lord, could stand?" and the text never names a group of super-faithful folks who would pass. He asks it as a question with no one to point to. That leaves everybody needing what comes next, which is "…with You there is forgiveness…" (Psalm 130:4).

The answer is forgiveness, friends. "But with You there is forgiveness, so that You may be feared." That little word "But" turns the whole song around. The question in verse 3 was heavy, and verse 4 gives the answer. I'll take forgiveness over a perfect record any day.

The answer is the LORD's word, friends. "I wait for the LORD; my soul does wait, and in His word I put my hope." His hope isn't in a feeling or a plan. It's in what the LORD has said. That's a solid place to stand while the oven timer is still running.

The answer is morning, friends. "My soul waits for the Lord more than watchmen wait for the morning…" Watchmen stand guard through the night, so I think morning is the thing they're counting on. He's saying his waiting is even more eager than theirs.

The answer is that loving devotion and redemption are with Him, friends. "…for with the LORD is loving devotion, and with Him is redemption in abundance." Notice the reason isn't about anything Israel did. It's about who the LORD is and what is with Him. Redemption in ABUNDANCE, friends. That's not a stingy batch.

The answer is True, friends. "And He will redeem Israel from all iniquity." Look at that word "all." After a song that started in the depths, it ends with the LORD redeeming and no iniquity left out. That's a long way up from the bottom.

The answer is proud, friends. David says, "My heart is not proud, O LORD, my eyes are not haughty." He's telling the LORD where his heart stands, and that's some humble talk. Me, I'd have been tempted to mention the hat.

The answer is False, friends. David says, "I do not aspire to great things or matters too lofty for me." He's not reaching for things beyond him. And he says it straight to the LORD, which makes it even better.

The answer is a weaned child with his mother, friends. David says, "like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me." It's a quiet picture, a child who is simply with his mother. I think that's about as calm as a soul can look.

The answer is both now and forevermore, friends. David closes with "O Israel, put your hope in the LORD, both now and forevermore." That covers today and every day after. Hope with no expiration date beats any coupon I've ever seen.
